hypothesis: Build point-in-time eligible universe
change: Added auditable classification and investability rules plus 20-trading-day target
motivation: Establish a leakage-safe research panel before signals
metric: Panel validation
result: 21104236 panel rows; 8399139 eligible; 8321030 eligible with target
notes: 2024-2025 remains final test only; target is censored if 20 later returns are incomplete

hypothesis: Medium-term momentum (skip most recent 20 days) predicts positive 20-day forward cross-sectional returns
change: Added mom_120_20 factor and the reusable single-factor evaluation harness (IC, deciles, rank autocorrelation, coverage, non-overlapping 20-day long-short with turnover and costs)
motivation: First vertical slice of Week 2; establishes the template applied identically to the other five signals
metric: Mean Spearman IC; Newey-West(20) t-stat; gross/net Sharpe at 1/5/10/20 bps
result: Mean rank IC -0.00002 (NW t=-0.00); mean Pearson IC 0.0056 (NW t=0.73); decile returns non-monotonic (hump peaking at D3); rank autocorr 0.987 (1d) / 0.768 (20d); turnover 0.895 per rebalance; gross Sharpe 0.188; net Sharpe 0.178/0.138/0.088/-0.011 at 1/5/10/20bp; breakeven ~19bp; -41.6% worst period in the 2009 momentum crash
decision: Keep in the six-signal set as a documented null; do not re-tune the window; do not treat as a standalone strategy
notes: 2024-2025 sealed: last evaluated date 2023-11-30 so no target window reaches into 2024. Memo: reports/factor_memo_01_momentum.md

hypothesis: Recent five-day losers outperform over the next 20 days
change: Added rev_5 = -sum of the last five daily returns
motivation: Plan 5.2 short-term reversal
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC +0.0077 (t=2.12); deciles rise monotonically D1-D9 then D10 collapses; turnover 1.74; gross Sharpe 0.149; breakeven 6.0bp; net Sharpe -0.108 at 10bp
decision: Keep with caution: does not survive Bonferroni across the six tests, and offset spread is -0.32 to +0.55
notes: Long-short book longs D10, the one decile that breaks the pattern

hypothesis: High realized volatility predicts lower 20-day returns
change: Added rvol_20 = sqrt(sum of squared returns over t-20..t-1)
motivation: Plan 5.3 realized volatility
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Signed rank IC +0.0286 (t=-2.85 raw, correct direction); effect is concentrated in D10 at 0.45% vs 0.94% interior peak; turnover 1.22; gross Sharpe 0.161; breakeven 14.0bp; net Sharpe 0.047 at 10bp
decision: Keep as the strongest single candidate; survives Bonferroni
notes: D1 is below the interior peak, so this is a short of high volatility rather than a low-volatility premium

hypothesis: Abnormally high volume predicts higher 20-day returns
change: Added vs_20 = log(turnover_t / mean turnover over t-20..t-1)
motivation: Plan 5.4 volume surprise
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC +0.0056 (t=3.43, most significant of the six); gross Sharpe 0.344; turnover 1.84; breakeven 5.6bp; net Sharpe -0.273 at 10bp
decision: Keep, but record that it is statistically real and economically unusable on its own
notes: Turnover rather than share volume, because price/volume/shares are as-traded in this export and a split cancels out of the turnover ratio

hypothesis: Momentum in market-model residuals predicts higher 20-day returns
change: Added rmom_120_20: OLS on 252 days ending t-21, residuals summed over t-120..t-21 in closed form
motivation: Plan 5.5 residual momentum
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC -0.0036 (t=-0.63), wrong sign, negative in 12 of 18 years; gross Sharpe 0.059; breakeven 3.7bp; coverage 98.98% with 20 zero-coverage dates in Jan 2006 because the factor needs 273 days of history
decision: Keep only for the Week 5 ablation
notes: Residualising did not rescue momentum; it removed what little was left

hypothesis: Stocks near their 252-day high outperform stocks in deep drawdown
change: Added dd_252 on the cumulative total-return index, not on price
motivation: Plan 5.6 drawdown
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC +0.0150 (t=1.39, insignificant); hump-shaped deciles, D1 0.60% and D10 0.67% against an interior peak of 0.98%; turnover 1.00; gross Sharpe 0.032; breakeven 3.6bp
notes: Measured on returns because price is not split-adjusted in this export

hypothesis: Portfolio statistics are sensitive to the rebalance offset and to the drawdown convention
change: Averaged all 20 rebalance offsets instead of one; floored the drawdown peak at starting wealth 1.0
motivation: A single-offset book gave rev_5 a negative gross Sharpe despite a significantly positive IC
metric: Gross Sharpe mean and spread across the 20 offsets
result: Offset spread is widest for the high-turnover factors: rev_5 -0.315 to +0.547, vs_20 0.065 to 0.630. Momentum gross Sharpe 0.188 -> 0.147 and breakeven ~19bp -> ~14.9bp
decision: Adopt offset averaging as the standard convention; supersede the portfolio numbers in W2-001
notes: Estimator change only; no factor was re-tuned and 2024-2025 remains sealed

hypothesis: Volume surprise and drawdown require same-close execution unless their inputs are lagged one day
change: Lagged vs_20 to turnover at t-1 against t-21..t-2, and dd_252 to the drawdown at t-1 against the peak over t-252..t-1; strengthened the shared leakage test to perturb row t itself
motivation: The target runs from the close of t, so a signal needing t's own close could only be executed at the instant the return starts accruing
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross Sharpe; breakeven cost
result: vs_20 signed IC 0.0056->0.0039, NW t 3.43->2.50, gross Sharpe 0.344->0.256, breakeven 5.6bp->4.1bp, no longer survives Bonferroni across six tests. dd_252 nearly unchanged: t 1.39->1.44, gross Sharpe 0.032->0.044
decision: Adopt the lagged definitions; all six factors are now determined by the close of t-1
notes: About a third of the volume-surprise IC was an execution assumption. rvol_20 is now the only factor surviving the multiple-testing correction.

hypothesis: The six factors are not six independent bets
change: Built the aligned six-factor rank panel and measured cross-sectional rank and daily portfolio-return correlations
motivation: Week 2 decile shapes suggested momentum, volatility, drawdown and residual momentum share one distressed/high-volatility exposure
metric: Mean daily rank correlation; daily gross portfolio-return correlation
result: rmom vs mom: rank 0.73, returns 0.76. rvol vs dd: rank -0.48 but returns +0.87. mom vs dd returns 0.75. Only rev_5 and vs_20 are distinct; vs_20's book has no return correlation above 0.17
decision: Treat the four as one cluster; let Week 4 models set weights rather than assuming an equal composite
notes: Return correlation is the informative measure: mom and rvol look independent by rank (-0.10) but their books correlate 0.46

hypothesis: Walk-forward folds must be purged by the target horizon
change: Added ten fixed expanding-window folds with a 20-trading-day purge before each validation year
motivation: An observation at t carries a target to t+20, so training to the boundary trains on validation-year returns
metric: Fold structure; purge length
result: Ten folds, train 1973 to 4239 days, exactly 20 trading days purged in every fold, final validation stops 2023-11-30
notes: No fold can reach the sealed period

hypothesis: A dollar-neutral rank-weighted book is a usable baseline
change: Built the capped, dollar-neutral, 20-day staggered-cohort portfolio with daily P&L, turnover, costs and exposures
motivation: Week 2's single-offset rebalance was an unstable estimator; staggered cohorts use every start date at once
metric: Gross/net Sharpe; turnover; breakeven; market beta
result: Composite gross Sharpe 0.121, breakeven 8.7bp, net -0.018 at 10bp. Nothing clears 10bp. Position cap never binds (largest position 0.35% vs 1% cap). Fast signals self-cancel across cohorts: gross exposure 0.39-0.44 for vs_20 and rev_5
notes: Dollar-neutral is not beta-neutral: rvol beta -0.34, dd -0.28, composite -0.23, negative in every rolling window

hypothesis: Rank-continuous weights capture more of these signals than tail deciles
change: Ran both weightings through the identical staggered-cohort estimator so the comparison isolates the weighting
motivation: Week 2 argued rank weights should help because five of six factors have hump-shaped deciles
metric: Gross Sharpe and turnover under each weighting
result: REJECTED. Decile weighting wins 5 of 7 on gross Sharpe and 6 of 7 on turnover. Best net book overall is the decile composite: Sharpe 0.001 at 10bp and 10.1bp breakeven, vs -0.018 and 8.7bp for rank
decision: Keep rank weighting as the pre-declared Week 4 baseline anyway, and carry both forward
notes: The Week 2 mechanism was right but the conclusion backwards: rank weights do not avoid the broken tail buckets, they add the low-signal middle 80% and its turnover. Switching the baseline after seeing the winner would be the degrees-of-freedom problem the protocol prevents.

hypothesis: A model fitted on the six factor ranks forecasts the 20-day cross-sectional return better than an equal-weighted composite
change: Added src/models/walk_forward.py: OLS, Ridge and HistGradientBoosting fitted independently in each of the ten folds
motivation: Week 3 showed the composite loads mostly on one correlated cluster; a fitted model can reweight toward the independent signals
training_window: Expanding, 2006-02-01 to each fold train_end (3.0M to 6.9M rows)
validation_window: Ten fixed folds, 2014-2023, 4293065 scored rows per model
metric: Out-of-sample R2, Pearson IC, rank IC with Newey-West t at 20 lags
result: OOS R2 negative for all three (-0.00065 ols, -0.00065 ridge, -0.00042 gbm); rank IC 0.0220 ols (t 8.82), 0.0221 ridge (t 8.59), 0.0197 gbm (t 7.74)
notes: No point-prediction skill; the entire edge is in cross-sectional ordering. gbm has the highest Pearson IC and the lowest rank IC. LightGBM not installed; sklearn histogram booster used instead

hypothesis: Model-driven books beat the pre-registered composite net of costs
change: Fed each model's predictions through the unchanged Week 3 staggered-cohort backtest under rank and decile weighting
motivation: A significant IC does not imply a tradable book; Week 2 already found one case where it did not
validation_window: Ten folds concatenated into one continuous 2014-2023 daily series, 2496 days
metric: Gross and net Sharpe at 1/5/10/20 bp, breakeven bp, turnover, beta, max drawdown
result: Composite gross Sharpe 0.333 and breakeven 25.0 bp beats every model; best model gbm__decile 0.174 and 10.5 bp; ols and ridge net-negative at 10 bp
notes: Null result. Models trade more for less: ols earns 0.74% gross on a 0.70 book at 6.8x turnover against the composite's 2.81% on a 0.90 book at 5.6x

hypothesis: The Week 3 headline is a valid comparison bar for Week 4
change: Recomputed the composite through identical per-fold machinery restricted to the 2014-2023 validation dates
motivation: Comparing a 2014-2023 model against a 2006-2023 baseline would be a window artefact, not a result
training_window: None; the composite is not fitted
metric: Gross Sharpe and breakeven bp on matched dates, plus t-statistics on sub-period difference
result: Composite gross Sharpe 0.121 over 2006-2023 becomes 0.333 over 2014-2023; breakeven 8.7 bp becomes 25.0 bp; reproduces the Week 3 daily series to 1e-16
notes: The 0.147 / 10.1 bp target in PROGRESS.md was stale. Sub-period Sharpe difference is +0.441 with SE 0.477 (t 0.92): no evidence the decades differ. Every book in the study has |t| <= 1.06 against zero

hypothesis: Inner-validation MSE identifies the Ridge penalty
change: Probed the alpha grid beyond its pre-registered upper bound and measured the effect on the cross-sectional ordering
motivation: The search returned the grid maximum in all ten folds, which means the grid, not the data, chose the value
metric: Inner MSE across alpha, and mean daily cross-sectional Spearman correlation between prediction sets
result: MSE falls monotonically out to alpha 1e10 for a total 0.005% improvement; predictions at alpha 1e4 and 1e10 correlate only 0.86 by daily rank
decision: Keep the pre-registered grid, change the criterion in Week 5
notes: MSE cannot identify the alpha yet the alpha materially changes the portfolio: ridge rotates coefficients rather than scaling them, so momentum's loading flips sign. Not retuned after the fact, by protocol

hypothesis: The 20-day warm-up block used to pre-ramp each fold's book is safe
change: Removed the warm-up: predictions and cohorts are validation-only, and the ten folds run as one continuous 2014-2023 backtest with cohorts carrying across annual model changes
motivation: A model fit through train_end has already seen the returns realised during train_end+1..train_end+20, which is exactly the warm-up window, so cohorts formed there trade on look-ahead
training_window: Unchanged, expanding to each fold train_end
validation_window: 2014-01-03 to 2023-12-29, one continuous 2515-day series, all eight books on an identical date index
metric: Gross Sharpe before and after removing the warm-up
result: Model books fell 31-43% of gross Sharpe (gbm__decile 0.174 to 0.099); composite fell 11% (0.333 to 0.297), which is the ramp window and year-end tails alone since it depends on no fitted model
notes: Withdrew the first version's portfolio numbers. Prediction IC/R2 unaffected: scored rows were never in the warm-up. Also fixed an unintended per-fold cohort reset that truncated year-end tail P&L. Composite reproduces the Week 3 daily series exactly except the 19 ramp days. Regression test added

hypothesis: Sharpe x sqrt(years) is adequate inference for these books
change: Replaced portfolio t-statistics with Newey-West HAC at 20 lags on mean daily gross return, reporting both
motivation: 20 staggered daily cohorts induce serial dependence in the daily series, so the naive statistic overstates precision
metric: HAC t-statistic at 20 lags versus naive Sharpe x sqrt(years)
result: Composite HAC t 1.01 (naive 0.94); every model book 0.26-0.32; the two statistics agree to within 0.07 everywhere
notes: The correction is mild here but the verdict is unchanged and now defensible: no book in the study, baseline included, is distinguishable from zero. Ridge deliberately not retuned; rank-IC selection deferred to Week 5 as a declared training-only robustness experiment

hypothesis: CRSP SICCD in this export is point-in-time, not a backfilled header field
change: Audited SICCD against the SecInfoStartDt/SecInfoEndDt interval records on the raw export before using it
motivation: Week 1 already found SecurityActiveFlg unusable point-in-time; sector must be audited the same way before it is trusted
training_window: Not applicable; structural audit of 96,826 security-info records
metric: Distinct SICCD per PERMNO, header-row agreement, sentinel rate
result: 12,079 of 21,548 PERMNOs carry more than one SICCD over time, tied to SecInfo intervals, so it is not backfilled. Header row matches the first interval more often (7,420) than the last (3,137), so the header must not be used. 9,535 of 96,826 rows (9.8%) are sentinel 0/9999/empty, clustering on end-of-life stubs
decision: Use SICCD via the interval join only
notes: PRE-DECLARED before any neutralisation result was seen. Limitation: time-varying structure shows the field is not uniformly backfilled but cannot prove a reclassification was recorded when publicly known rather than at its effective date. Sentinel codes carry the prior interval forward, never a later one

hypothesis: Point-in-time sector, rolling beta and log market cap can be built as t-1 exposures without leakage
change: Build src/features/exposures.py: SIC-division sector from the interval join, rolling market beta over the existing 252-day estimation window ending t-1, and log market cap at t-1
motivation: Neutralisation requires exposures known at the same moment as the factors themselves, which is the close of t-1
metric: Coverage on the aligned panel, and a leakage test perturbing every input at or after t
result: PRE-DECLARED, not yet run
notes: Sector granularity fixed in advance at roughly 12 groups: 81 two-digit SIC groups against ~1,660 names per date is ~20 per bucket, too thin for stable residualisation. Every exposure must pass the same at-or-after-t perturbation test the six factors pass

hypothesis: Cross-sectionally residualising scores against sector, beta and size improves risk-adjusted net performance
change: Residualise the composite and each model score per date against the three exposures, then rerun the unchanged continuous backtest
motivation: Week 3 and Week 4 both found every book carries a persistent short market beta (-0.14 to -0.27) and loads on one correlated cluster, so no result so far can be called alpha
metric: Raw versus neutralised rank IC, HAC t, turnover, realised beta, net Sharpe at 1/5/10/20 bp, breakeven
result: PRE-DECLARED, not yet run
notes: Success is declared in advance as: realised market beta materially closer to zero AND net Sharpe at 10 bp no worse than the raw book. Neutralisation that only lowers beta by destroying return is a failure, not a win. Both rank and decile weighting carried

hypothesis: Each of the six factors contributes to the composite
change: Leave-one-out ablation: rebuild the composite six times, each dropping one factor, through the identical estimator
motivation: Week 3 found rmom is 0.76 correlated with mom by portfolio return and rvol/dd books correlate 0.87; if those are duplicates the composite may be carrying redundant turnover
training_window: Not applicable; the composite is not fitted
metric: Gross and net Sharpe, HAC t, turnover, breakeven per ablated composite
result: PRE-DECLARED, not yet run
notes: Interpretation fixed in advance: dropping a factor that leaves net Sharpe unchanged or better means that factor is redundant, not that it is harmful. No factor will be dropped on ablation evidence alone unless the full specification lock in W5-006 selects it

hypothesis: Results are stable across volatility regimes, sub-periods, cost assumptions and rebalance frequency
change: Split the continuous series by trailing market-volatility tercile and by sub-period, sweep costs, and rerun at a limited set of rebalance horizons
motivation: Every headline so far has a HAC t near or below 1.0, so apparent performance could be concentrated in one regime or one horizon choice
metric: Sharpe and HAC t within each regime and sub-period, cost curve, Sharpe by rebalance horizon
result: PRE-DECLARED, not yet run
notes: Rebalance horizons limited to a small pre-declared set to avoid a horizon search. A specification is not called robust because one slice looks good; the reported statistic is the dispersion across slices

hypothesis: One final specification can be locked before the sealed period is opened
change: Select a single book -- weighting, neutralisation and factor set -- and freeze it
motivation: Week 6 opens 2024-2025 exactly once; the specification must be fixed beforehand or the final test is not a test
validation_window: Locked before any 2024-2025 observation is read
metric: Declared before selection: net Sharpe at 10 bp on 2014-2023, subject to realised beta within 0.10 of zero
result: PRE-DECLARED, not yet run
notes: Selection rule is fixed here in advance so it cannot be chosen after seeing W5-003 to W5-005. If no book satisfies the beta constraint, the constraint is reported as unmet rather than relaxed to admit a winner

hypothesis: Result for W5-002
change: Built src/features/exposures.py and data/processed/exposures/
motivation: See W5-002
metric: Coverage on the aligned panel and an at-or-after-t leakage test
result: 100.0% coverage for sector, beta_252 and log_mcap on all 8,319,133 aligned rows; 9-11 sectors per date; 454 rows carried a sentinel sector forward; five tests pass including the perturbation test
notes: Complete coverage is not luck: Week 1 eligibility already requires 252 prior returns, exactly what the beta window needs. beta_252 spans -10.9 to +7.1, so it and log_mcap are winsorised at 1/99 before being regressed against

hypothesis: Result for W5-003
change: Residualised the composite and all three model scores per date against sector, beta and size, then reran the unchanged continuous backtest
motivation: See W5-003
metric: Pre-declared: beta materially closer to zero AND net Sharpe at 10 bp no worse than raw
result: FAIL in 7 of 8 books. Every book shed 75-98% of realised beta, so leg one passes everywhere; leg two fails because net Sharpe at 10 bp worsens. Only composite__decile passes both (beta -0.266 to -0.057, net@10bp +0.155 to +0.209, gross 0.297 to 0.486, HAC t 0.99 to 1.53)
notes: Mechanism: neutralisation halves annualised volatility (8.43% to 4.12%) while turnover and dollar cost drag stay flat (5.64x to 5.72x; 1.13% to 1.14%), so a fixed cost is charged against half the risk budget. Not levered away, since net Sharpe is leverage-invariant. Judged on gross Sharpe alone ols and ridge nearly tripled and this would have been logged as a win

hypothesis: Result for W5-004
change: Leave-one-out ablation over the six factors, both weightings
motivation: See W5-004
metric: Gross and net Sharpe, HAC t, turnover, breakeven per ablated composite
result: Redundant by the pre-declared rule: rmom_120_20 and vs_20. Not redundant: mom_120_20 and rev_5. Inconclusive: rvol_20 and dd_252, which help one weighting and hurt the other. Every ablated book sits at HAC |t| 0.81 to 1.29
notes: Of the mom/rmom pair Week 3 found 0.76-correlated, momentum is the half the composite needs and residual momentum is the spare, matching Week 4's exposure table (0.471 against 0.355)

hypothesis: Result for W5-005
change: Volatility-tercile, sub-period, cost and rebalance-horizon splits
motivation: See W5-005
metric: Sharpe and HAC t per slice; cost curve; Sharpe, turnover and breakeven per horizon
result: Low-vol tercile HAC t 2.43 and calendar 2018 t 2.21, both best-of-many ex-post slices and neither treated as a finding. Cost breakeven reproduces at 22.2 bp rank and 20.9 bp decile. Across horizons {5,10,20,40} gross Sharpe moves only 0.297-0.383 and HAC t stays 1.00-1.27, but breakeven swings 10.4 to 38.5 bp
notes: The breakeven figure quoted throughout this project is fragile to an arbitrary holding-period choice, swinging 3.7x, driven by turnover falling fivefold. Tercile boundaries are full-sample quantiles, so the regime split is descriptive and not implementable in real time

hypothesis: Result for W5-006
change: Applied the pre-declared selection rule mechanically to all 28 candidate books from Weeks 3-5
motivation: See W5-006
validation_window: Locked before any 2024-2025 observation is read
metric: Pre-declared: max net Sharpe at 10 bp subject to realised beta within 0.10 of zero
result: Only 8 of 28 books pass the beta constraint and all 8 are neutralised. Locked composite__decile__neutral: realised beta -0.057, gross Sharpe 0.486 (HAC t 1.53), net Sharpe at 10 bp +0.209
notes: Three raw ablated composites with competitive net Sharpe (+0.183, +0.183, +0.174) were disqualified on beta alone, which is what the constraint was written to do. The lock is a procedural commitment, not a claim of edge: HAC t 1.53 is p about 0.13, the best in the program and still not significant, and the winner is the maximum of 8 correlated admissible estimates with no multiple-testing correction

hypothesis: The W5-006 candidate grid gave the factor-set dimension a genuine chance to compete
change: Generated the 12 missing neutralised leave-one-out composites and reapplied the unchanged W5-006 rule from a programmatic candidate table
motivation: The rule varies weighting, neutralisation and factor set, but only raw ablations were ever evaluated, and every raw ablation fails the beta constraint, so factor set could not compete
metric: Pre-declared W5-006 rule, unchanged: max net Sharpe at 10 bp subject to |realised beta| <= 0.10
result: Grid went from 28 candidates with 8 admissible to 40 with 20; all 12 neutralised ablations pass the beta constraint where no raw ablation did. The winner CHANGED from composite__neutral__decile (net@10bp +0.209) to drop_rmom_120_20__neutral__decile (+0.238, beta -0.056, gross 0.534, HAC t 1.65)
notes: The rule was not modified, only applied to a complete grid. Margin over runner-up is 0.0103 and the top four books span 0.209-0.238, so the choice among them is inside the noise. The runner-up has the higher HAC t (1.97 vs 1.65): the rule selects on net Sharpe, not significance, as pre-registered. Completing the grid makes the selection statistically weaker, since the winner is now the max of 20 correlated admissible estimates rather than 8

hypothesis: The Week 6 protocol is fully determined and cannot be run by accident
change: Built src/evaluation/week6_final.py, which reads the lock file at runtime, hardcodes no book, and validates against a pre-2024 replay
motivation: A lock file naming a winner does not determine a run; unstated defaults would let the final test differ from the locked specification
metric: Replay reproduction of the locked book's recorded Week 5 figures, and refusal behaviour
result: Replay reproduces realised beta, gross Sharpe, net Sharpe at 10 bp, HAC t and max drawdown to about 1e-15. Sealed mode requires the literal string run-sealed-2024-2025-exactly-once; no argument exits before any data is opened
notes: Refuses on a missing field, a factor sign disagreeing with FACTOR_SIGN, a recorded commit that is not an ancestor of HEAD, or an uncommitted src/ on the sealed path. Commit equality was rejected as a check because it is unsatisfiable: the lock file lives in the repo, so the commit containing it cannot equal the hash recorded inside it

hypothesis: 2024-2025 was literally untouched during Weeks 1-5
change: Restricted the exposure audit summary to dates through 2023-11-30 and disclosed the earlier full-history summary
motivation: Exposures are built over full history because a t-1 rolling beta needs it, but the first audit summarised coverage and sector counts over 2024-2025 covariate rows
metric: Whether any sealed-period statistic was computed or displayed
result: Covariate summaries did span 2024-2025; no return, target or performance figure from the sealed period was ever computed. The winsorisation quantiles came from a beta range measured on a query restricted to dates through 2023-11-30, not from the full-history summary
decision: Disclose, do not claim an untouched seal
notes: The correct description is outcome-sealed, not untouched. Audit now ends at 2023-11-30 (aligned rows 7,351,850; exposure rows 19,107,452) and the module docstring states why summarising over full history is itself a leak of covariate distributions

hypothesis: The frozen Week 6 runner would execute the locked specification correctly on the sealed period
change: Fixed four blocking defects found in review before the sealed run: formation start, cohort cutoff, exactly-once enforcement and provenance authentication
motivation: A runner that merely names the right book does not execute the right test; each defect would have produced a plausible-looking but wrong final number
validation_window: Replay over 2014-01-02 to 2023-11-30, P&L to 2023-12-29; sealed period never executed
metric: Derived dates against the panel calendar, refusal behaviour, and replay reproduction
result: P0: formation start inherited walk_forward_splits' default first validation year of 2014, so the sealed run would have evaluated 2014-2025 and reported ten in-sample years as the held-out test; now read off the panel as the first trading date on or after 2024-01-01 (2024-01-02) and asserted. P1: hardcoded cutoff 2025-11-30 is a Sunday resolving to 2025-11-28, two cohorts short; now derived as pnl_end_tdi - hold_days = 2025-12-02. P1: exactly-once now enforced by an O_CREAT|O_EXCL marker written before any sealed data is opened. P1: provenance now also covers the lock JSON and requires the runner's content at the recorded commit to be byte-identical to the executing file
decision: Fix, commit, relock, hold for review
notes: Replay unchanged at formation 2014-01-02 and cutoff 2023-11-30, still reproducing all five recorded Week 5 figures, so the fixes did not perturb the validation baseline. Rank IC now drops nulls explicitly with per-metric date coverage recorded, since forward_return_20d is absent for the last ~20 formation dates of 2025 and would otherwise become a silent NaN. 71 tests pass

hypothesis: The locked specification is authenticated against the code that will execute it
change: Committed the corrected runner (d326f25), regenerated the lock from the unchanged candidate table, and committed the relock (f60f075)
motivation: Commit equality is unsatisfiable because the lock lives in the repo, and ancestry alone does not prove the executing code is the frozen code
metric: Winner and figures after regeneration; the three provenance guards
result: Regeneration is deterministic: same winner drop_rmom_120_20__neutral__decile, same net Sharpe at 10 bp 0.2379, same beta -0.0562, same 40 candidates with 20 admissible, with the recorded commit moved to d326f25. All three guards now pass -- ancestry, clean src/ and lock, and byte-identical runner at the recorded commit
decision: Ready for the sealed run, pending review
notes: No final artifact or run marker exists; 2024-2025 performance is still unevaluated

hypothesis: The specification locked in Week 5 forecasts 20-day cross-sectional returns out of sample, net of costs
change: Opened the sealed 2024-2025 period exactly once and ran drop_rmom_120_20__neutral__decile unchanged
motivation: A specification chosen on 2014-2023 evidence is untested until it is run once, as declared, on data never evaluated
training_window: 2014-2023 evidence only; nothing refitted for this run
validation_window: 2024-01-02 to 2025-12-02 formation; P&L 2024-01-03 to 2025-12-31; 501 days; rank IC on 482 formation dates
metric: Gross and net Sharpe with Newey-West HAC t at 20 lags, breakeven bp, turnover, realised beta, max drawdown, rank IC
result: Gross Sharpe 1.522 (HAC t 2.76); net Sharpe 1.491/1.368/1.215/0.909 at 1/5/10/20 bp; breakeven 49.7 bp; realised beta -0.065; max drawdown -4.1%; annual turnover 8.86x; mean rank IC 0.0364 (HAC t 4.63)
notes: Run once at commit 084f5eb against the specification locked at fbbe574; marker sealed_run_started.json prevents repetition. Profitable at every cost tier and beta stayed inside the 0.10 constraint out of sample, which it had no obligation to do

hypothesis: The out-of-sample result is materially better than the in-sample estimate
change: Compared the sealed result against the same book's 2014-2023 figures
motivation: A tripling of Sharpe out of sample is a large favourable surprise and warrants more scepticism than a small one
metric: Difference in gross Sharpe with its standard error
result: Out-of-sample 1.522 against in-sample 0.534: difference +0.99, SE about 1.10, t about 0.90. Not significantly different. Approximate 95% interval on the out-of-sample Sharpe runs about -0.5 to 3.6
notes: The hypothesis test and the estimate say different things and both are correct: the mean return is distinguishable from zero (HAC t 2.76) while the magnitude is barely pinned down. Using 1.52 as a forward expectation would be unsupported. Selection is not corrected for: the book is the max of 20 admissible correlated candidates, which normally biases expected out-of-sample performance downward, so the upside surprise is not explained by selection

hypothesis: The W6-002 iid Sharpe-interval and iid-SE difference test are consistent with the headline HAC inference
change: Recomputed the Sharpe confidence interval and the selection-sample-vs-sealed difference test using HAC-consistent standard errors (SE = SR/t, inverting the headline Newey-West t)
motivation: Reviewer flagged that quoting an iid interval (-0.5 to 3.6) beside a HAC t of 2.76 and calling both correct was incoherent -- they rest on different, incompatible assumptions about serial dependence
metric: 95% CI on sealed Sharpe; t-stat of the selection-sample-vs-sealed Sharpe difference, both computed with HAC-consistent SE = SR/t in place of the iid SE = sqrt((1+SR^2/2)/years)
result: HAC 95% interval on sealed Sharpe is [0.44, 2.60] (SE 0.550), excluding zero, versus the iid sensitivity interval [-0.52, 3.56] (SE 1.042). The selection-sample-vs-sealed difference is t = 1.55 (SE 0.639) under HAC-consistent SEs, not the t = 0.90 (SE 1.10) reported in W6-002 under iid SEs
decision: Correct and supersede W6-002's interval and difference-test figures; W6-002's point estimates and its qualitative conclusion (not significantly better) are unchanged and stand
notes: This is a correction to how uncertainty was quantified, not to what was measured. The HAC interval governs because it is derived from the same test statistic as the headline result; the iid interval is kept in the report only as an explicitly labelled sensitivity check, since it ignores the autocorrelation the staggered 20-day cohorts induce. Neither the sealed result nor the decision to stop research changes
